note: The map of what there is to decide about. content/ontology.json is the navigation: what the catalogue can show today. This is the map: what there is to show at all. Coverage is the difference between them, published as a number rather than left as an impression. Authored in content/taxonomy/, compiled by pipeline/build_taxonomy.py, gated by research/taxonomy_audit.js.

realms.label: Food and drink
realms.edge: Everything eaten or drunk, where it is bought, and where it is eaten. Food grown at home belongs here; the tools for growing it belong to Home. Food for animals belongs to Animals. Infant formula belongs to Family and care, because the decision there is about feeding a baby, not about groceries.

decisions.label: Water at home
decisions.reason: The decision here is a water supplier or a filter, and both are already decisions in Home. This line exists so the map does not imply drinking water is only something you buy in a bottle.

decisions.label: Tobacco and cigarettes
decisions.reason: The catalogue ranks options inside a decision so a reader can choose a better one. There is no better cigarette on the axes this site measures, and building the comparison would dress a health decision as a values decision. Named here so its absence is a position rather than an oversight.

decisions.label: Vapes and nicotine pouches
decisions.reason: Same reason as tobacco. The environmental case for a rechargeable vape over a disposable one is real, and it belongs in a guide about waste rather than in a ranking that would read as a recommendation to buy either.

decisions.label: Independent restaurants and cafes
decisions.reason: Ranking individual local restaurants needs local data the catalogue does not have and could not keep fresh. The useful unit here is a guide to reading a menu and a kitchen, not a national league table.

decisions.label: Foraging
decisions.reason: There is nothing to compare and nothing to buy. This belongs in a guide, and it sits on the map so that the free way of getting food is visible next to the paid ones.

realms.label: Home
realms.edge: The place itself, what it runs on, what is in it, and what keeps it standing. Renting and buying belong here because where a person lives is the largest values decision most people ever make. The money instruments attached to a home, mortgages and home insurance, belong to Money. Food eaten in the home belongs to Food and drink.

families.label: Other ways to hold a home

decisions.label: Address change and utility switching services
Solar panels
decisions.reason: two real per-model registers exist, the UK's MCS Product Directory and California's CEC Solar Equipment List, but neither could be read with the tools available. MCS's search interface returns HTTP 403 to automated requests. The CEC list renders manufacturer, wattage, efficiency and PTC data through client-side JavaScript after the page loads, so a URL fetch retrieves only the empty filter form; its bulk data export exists only as a binary spreadsheet that no available tool can parse into rows. TUV Rheinland's Certipedia requires the same kind of interactive search. Building this decision honestly needs either browser automation that can drive one of those search interfaces to completion, or a spreadsheet reader for the CEC export; manufacturer datasheets alone, with no register to check them against, would not clear this lane's bar for a second, independent axis.

decisions.label: Bulky waste, reuse and tip services
Water boilers and filters at the tap
Robot lawn mowers and outdoor smart devices

realms.label: Clothing
realms.edge: What a person wears, and every way of getting it other than buying new. Washing clothes belongs to Home, because the decision there is a detergent. Children's clothing sits in Family and care, where the sizing and the hand-me-down question live together.

realms.label: Personal care
realms.edge: What goes on a body to keep it clean, comfortable and presentable. Medicines and treatments for a condition belong to Health, and the line between them is whether a person is treating something or maintaining something. Nappies and baby toiletries belong to Family and care.

realms.label: Health
realms.edge: Treating and monitoring a body, and the services that do it. The line against Personal care is treatment against maintenance. Health insurance belongs to Money. What a gym sells is here; what a person wears to it belongs to Clothing.

decisions.label: Blood glucose monitors and diabetes supplies
Abortion services and support
decisions.reason: This is a decision about access and care rather than a product to compare, and the honest instrument is a directory of what is lawful and available in a place, held by an organisation equipped to keep it accurate and safe. Named on the map so its absence is visible.

decisions.label: Earplugs, eye masks and white noise
Complementary and alternative therapies
decisions.reason: The catalogue can honestly compare a provider on price, ownership, data handling and complaints, and cannot rank a therapy that has no accepted evidence base without appearing to endorse it. Held until the measures can separate the provider from the claim.

realms.label: Transport
realms.edge: Getting a person or a thing from one place to another, and everything owned or paid for in order to do it. Car and travel insurance belong to Money. A holiday belongs to Travel; the train that gets you there is here.

families.label: Getting a car without buying one

decisions.label: Walking and wheeling routes
decisions.reason: There is no purchase and no provider to rank. It is on the map because a catalogue of how people move that starts at buying a car has already answered the question badly.

realms.label: Technology
realms.edge: Devices, the connections they run on, and the software and services used through them. Smart home devices belong to Home, because the decision is about the house. Streaming a film belongs to Media and culture; the television belongs here.

decisions.label: Desks, chairs and home office setup
AI training data and consent
decisions.reason: There is nothing here a reader buys, and the question of whose work a model was trained on decides several rankings elsewhere in the catalogue. It sits on the map as a measure to be applied to AI decisions rather than as a decision of its own.

decisions.label: Community forums and chat you host
Running a model on your own hardware

decisions.label: Data subject access and deletion tools

realms.label: Media and culture
realms.edge: What a person reads, watches, listens to, plays and makes, and the places that hold it. The device is Technology. Formal study is Learning. Libraries sit in Learning, where open knowledge is gathered.

decisions.label: Sports team ownership and supporter trusts
Betting and gambling services
decisions.reason: A ranking implies the reader should pick one, and there is no version of this that serves a person better than not starting. The catalogue's values axes would also flatter the largest operators, whose compliance teams are the best resourced. Named so the refusal is visible and arguable rather than silent.

realms.label: Learning
realms.edge: Formal study, self-teaching, and the open knowledge anyone can reach for free. Books read for pleasure belong to Media and culture. Student loans belong to Money. Childcare belongs to Family and care, because the decision there is about care rather than about a curriculum.

decisions.label: Open licensing and public domain tools

realms.label: Travel
realms.edge: Going somewhere and staying there. The daily commute belongs to Transport; the flight and the hotel belong here. Travel insurance and travel money belong to Money, and are named here so the map does not pretend a trip is only a booking.

decisions.label: Flight emissions and offsetting
decisions.reason: Offsetting is a contested product and the honest comparison is between flying and not flying, or between a flight and a train. The catalogue can rank offset providers on integrity, and will not do so until it can say plainly that buying one is not the same as not emitting.

decisions.label: Hotels
decisions.reason: State attorney general settlements over hidden resort fees, and government labor and ADA findings, are real but they measure who got caught rather than current conduct: they track a chain's size and visibility more than its behaviour, so an axis built only from them would have put unsued brands at the top of a column that reads as good. The honest primary measure is whether a chain's own booking flow shows the total price, mandatory fees included, at first display, which is checkable for every brand today rather than only the ones with a public record. It could not be gathered that way: the booking search or results page for ten of the twelve brands considered (Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, IHG, Choice, Motel 6, Red Roof Inn, Best Western, Extended Stay America, Radisson) returned an error to a plain fetch and to one with a full browser header, and only two (Wyndham, Omni) served a readable page at all, of which only Wyndham's said anything about fee inclusion. Held until that evidence can be gathered directly, in a browser, for most of the roster; the enforcement history remains worth keeping as a separate, clearly labelled record once the primary axis can carry its own weight.

decisions.label: Volunteering trips
decisions.reason: The sector contains real placements and real harm, and telling them apart needs local judgement the catalogue cannot supply from a distance. Held until a partner with that judgement can stand behind the comparison.

realms.label: Money
realms.edge: Holding money, moving it, borrowing it, growing it, and insuring against loss. Where a person banks decides what their money funds while they sleep, which is why this realm is small in spending and large in consequence. Buying a home belongs to Home; the mortgage belongs here.

decisions.label: Money management and open banking apps
Crypto mining and staking
decisions.reason: The measures that matter here are energy use and custody risk, and both change faster than the catalogue can currently keep a ranking honest. Held rather than published stale.

realms.label: Family and care
realms.edge: Looking after people who depend on you, at both ends of a life. Children's schooling belongs to Learning. What a household buys for itself belongs to Home. Here the decision is always made on someone else's behalf, which is why it is held apart.

realms.label: Animals
realms.edge: Animals a person lives with or acts on behalf of. Meat and dairy belong to Food and drink, where the decision is about eating. Wildlife feeding in a garden belongs to Home. Here the animal is the one being provided for.

decisions.label: Pet bird and small animal food
Breeders and sellers
decisions.reason: A ranking here would read as a shortlist of places to buy an animal, and the catalogue's position is that adoption comes first. What can be published honestly is what a lawful, welfare-first sale looks like, which is a guide rather than a comparison.

realms.label: Work and livelihood
realms.edge: The decisions a person makes as a worker, and the small number a very small organisation makes on people's behalf. COICOP does not classify these, because they are not household consumption. They are on the map because where a person works and who represents them shapes more of a life than most purchases do, and because a catalogue that only addresses a shopper has decided in advance that a person is only a shopper.

realms.label: Civic life and giving
realms.edge: Money, time and voice given rather than spent. COICOP counts what non-profits spend on households here; this realm counts it from the other end, as the decisions a person makes about where their giving and their participation go. Buying from a mission-driven company is not giving, and belongs to Organizations.

realms.label: Organizations
realms.edge: The same catalogue read by who owns and sells a thing rather than by what the thing is. It is deliberately not a purpose category, so nothing lives here that lives elsewhere: a phone is in Technology whoever makes it. This realm answers a different question, which is who a person wants to hand money to at all.
